title: Forces and Magnets (KS2)
subject: Science
strapline: Pushes, pulls, friction, gravity and how magnets work.
facts: A force is a push or a pull; forces can make things speed up, slow down, change direction or change shape.
Gravity is a force that pulls objects towards the Earth — it makes things fall.
Friction is a force between two surfaces that rub together; it slows moving things down.
Air resistance and water resistance are types of friction that act against movement.
A magnet has two poles: north and south.
Like poles repel (push apart); unlike (opposite) poles attract (pull together).
Magnets attract magnetic materials — iron, steel, nickel and cobalt — but not plastic, wood or paper.

quick_quiz.q: What force pulls a dropped ball to the ground?
Do two north poles attract or repel?

teacher_tips: Let children test which materials are magnetic before telling them.
Use the words attract/repel precisely — poles, not "sides".
Measure friction fairly: same ramp, different surfaces.
